title: Local image registration restores six Yale faces but yields seven matched quires
statement: The six examined archive-excluded Yale faces pass the original full-page geometry gates after smoothly regularized local correction. With both faces, same quire, exact folio span and the original orientation-specific tier rule, the sample grows from seven mates in six quires to nine mates in seven. Seven mates in six quires have disjoint controls. The alternate T control f103+f112 still cannot match f105+f114: rescued f103v scores 0.922 QC pixels at p90, while f105v scores 3.890 on its original archival split. The cutoff is 1.819996 QC pixels. A preliminary common-seed calculation reached eight quires, but exact reconstruction of the per-face seeds leaves seven. A calibration on 300 synthetic stroke crops passed the frozen clean and degraded gates. The width ratio is less reliable below three pixels. The eight-quire prerequisite for extracting and comparing the manuscript marker was not met.
check: Reproduce the six exact archive-seeded geometry rows from the linked assets. Establish independent landmarks or a spatial correspondence rule before checking more excluded Yale faces, then require full same-quire exact-span matching and eight independent quires. Use at least 20 anonymously validated native crops per face, both leaf faces, and report disjoint controls. Recover and compare the marker only once those criteria are met.

primary.role: Recover a disjoint exact-span control within quire E.
One verso required for the physical mate comparison in quire T.
The second verso required for that comparison in quire T.

backup.role: Evaluate separately as E sensitivity with an overlapping control.

geometry_plan.quality_metric_scale: Yale target longest side resized to 1600 pixels with INTER_AREA. Errors are QC pixels, not native pixels.
geometry_plan.registration_primary: Run unchanged archival SIFT correspondence generation and QC target sizing. Preserve the archival homography as baseline. Fit a fixed smoothly regularized local displacement against training correspondences only, initialized from its RANSAC homography. Compare both on the same deterministic spatially stratified held-out matches, without dropping large held-out errors. Report a whole local-region holdout sensitivity as well.
geometry_plan.registration_secondary: Check visibly matched anatomical and letter landmarks and NCC patch matches. Their results diagnose geometric uncertainty and do not determine archival error tiers.
geometry_plan.comparison: Preserve archive mate map, exact positive folio span, same quire, complete recto plus verso and matching unordered orientation-specific QC tiers. Report scan-geometric support, then support with independently validated crop eligibility. Require at least 8 informative quires for any primary marker comparison. Expose the disjoint sensitivity.
geometry_plan.selection_basis: Published baseline failed registration rows, a read-only exact-span coverage audit, public scan availability and leaf identities only. No manuscript marker values used.

geometry_extension_before_marker.phase: Secondary feasibility, after applying the unchanged procedure to the primary roster and before any manuscript width measurement
geometry_extension_before_marker.question: Do the independently identified alternative exact-span controls supplied by restoration of f103v and f105v have matched quality tiers under the frozen archive cutoff?
geometry_extension_before_marker.acceptance: Apply the same frozen registration and quality gates. Both new faces may fall in either tier, but must jointly create the fully matched mate f105+f114 against disjoint control f103+f112, and any remaining primary marker test is conditional on a verified crop-level floor. Never modify individual error tiers or change the algorithms to reach the cutoff.

prerequisites.geometric_roster: Apply the unchanged archive pair map, exact positive folio span, same-quire requirement, complete recto and verso, and frozen orientation-specific geometry tiers. Use only pairs and controls in the geometry table from the six rescues. A historically admitted face remains usable only when its recreated archived homography passes the same gates and reproduces its original tier.
prerequisites.photo_acquisition: Only the registered Yale scan on both faces of every leaf. Do not pool Voyager or cropped images from different acquisitions.

box_sampling.input: Archive companion coordinates only. Remove all text strings and use fixed native rectangles from image-only registration.
box_sampling.geometry: Take archive-style 1 companion pixel padding, project to native, round outward, and keep only full in-image crops whose centers are inside the accepted matching hull. Never rescale the output crop. Use a fixed pseudorandom sample of at most 96 boxes per face chosen by face and box coordinates before measuring.
box_sampling.blindness: Render anonymous native grayscale crops and withhold the quire, leaf, mate labels, handles and page IDs from the extractor. Record geometry validity separately and keep the pair table and page-to-anonymous-ID crosswalk for the scoring stage.

endpoint.crop: Equal selected ink-component centerline points, median twice the Euclidean distance to the background divided by selected component height. Use the frozen synthetic-calibration retention and segmentation rules on native grayscale crops.
endpoint.leaf: Arithmetic mean of its two face medians.
endpoint.pair: Absolute difference between the two leaf summaries.
endpoint.mate: Mate discrepancy minus unweighted mean discrepancy of its eligible matched nonmates.
endpoint.quire: Unweighted mean mate effect over retained mate rows in that quire.
endpoint.estimate: Unweighted mean of the retained quire effects. Negative favors closer physical mates.

synthetic_marker_plan.statistic: Enumerate all 2^q quire sign flips at q >= 8 and report the exact lower-tail fraction with comparison inclusive of ties. This checks a symmetric quire-effect null. No independence assumption is applied to multiple mate rows or overlapping controls within a quire.
synthetic_marker_plan.without_disjoint_controls: Report the primary estimate only when its prespecified support floor is reached; independently report the alternative retaining only disjoint controls, with no p-value for any sensitivity under eight quires. Show the matched counts and any exclusions in either case.
synthetic_marker_plan.calibration_limit: Measurements at true widths below 3 native pixels are more biased in calibration. Quantify calibration behavior and retain the fixed crop quality rules. Do not filter manuscript crops by the endpoint, an estimated stroke width, or the sign of the effect.
synthetic_marker_plan.scope: Geometry and dimensionless image-based stroke width. No ink, quill, author, chemical or material attribution follows.

evidence.matching_split: The published extraction driver supplies 440908 plus one-based index in the 181-face Yale manifest. The same held-out descriptor matches are used for the rerun homography and the local fit. The archived published homography and its rerun are reported separately, since changing RANSAC runtime can produce a different baseline fit. A single seed used in initial feasibility work is preserved as a sensitivity. It is ineligible for scoring the comparison with the fixed design.

f33v.description: Source landmarks visually selected before comparison with automatic registration. Physical correspondence checked using paired crops. Target centers based on local high-pass normalized cross-correlation with subpixel peak interpolation. Residuals quantify agreement between independent point estimates and automatic model. They do not replace the held-out automatic control metric.

f108v.description: Source landmarks visually selected before comparison with automatic registration. Physical correspondence checked using paired crops. Target centers based on local high-pass normalized cross-correlation with subpixel peak interpolation. Residuals quantify agreement between independent point estimates and automatic model. They do not replace the held-out automatic control metric.

rows.name: red star alongside long second paragraph
tall slash at end of line

f111v.description: Source landmarks visually selected before comparison with automatic registration. Physical correspondence checked using paired crops. Target centers based on local high-pass normalized cross-correlation with subpixel peak interpolation. Residuals quantify agreement between independent point estimates and automatic model. They do not replace the held-out automatic control metric.

f105v.scope: Right-margin visual registration audit. No manuscript width measurements.
f105v.method: Eight source centers were selected by eye before reading the fit. The seed fit supplied the center of a plus-or-minus 55 native pixel search, and its coarse homography supplied local patch orientation and scaling. A high-pass normalized cross-correlation chose native target peaks with quadratic subpixel refinement. Candidate locations were verified in wide paired crops extending beyond the matching patch. Main patch size was 99 by 99 native pixels, with 71 and 125 pixel sensitivity checks.
f105v.dependence_and_limits: Target searching is initialized from the same registration being checked and its coarse homography sets the patch geometry. This bounds what the audit can detect and is not an independent global registration or a formal held-out test. Selection favors distinctive right-margin ink and should not be used to estimate a page-wide error rate. Ambiguous centers are excluded. Reported coordinates are approximate local patch estimates.

landmarks.description: first-line tall fork near right edge
landmarks.visual_note: The same fork and two looped marks above it are visible in both scans. The secondary peak moves to the preceding stroke.

landmarks.description: small hooked stroke above the next line
landmarks.visual_note: The narrow and main patches match the hooked mark at the end of the same sequence. The widest patch shifts about 9 native pixels toward the adjacent repeated short stroke.
The same isolated tall crossbar and terminal loop match. The secondary peak is a false lock on a different row.

landmarks.description: upper-right tall stem with adjoining loop
landmarks.visual_note: Two almost equal peaks, also favored by different patch sizes, fall on different parts of the neighboring upright strokes. The paired views identify the same glyph group, but the exact source center cannot be placed confidently.

landmarks.description: tall fork near cropped right edge
landmarks.visual_note: The same upright fork and the preceding hook match. The alternative peak moves onto the terminal loop of the fork.
The same rounded loop, descender and preceding hooked mark match. The alternative peak shifts to the adjoining word.

landmarks.description: tall fork above right edge cluster
landmarks.visual_note: The same fork below the paired looped forms and above the long horizontal connector matches. The main peak best aligns the junction. The first peaks from three patch sizes vary by about 2.7 native pixels.

landmarks.description: right edge rising fork near bottom paragraph
landmarks.visual_note: The paired views identify the same neighboring fork, but the two main peaks have nearly equal scores and fall on opposite sides of the junction. The smaller patch picks the alternative peak.

supplementary_geometry_only.visual_landmark_note: The landmark positions were visually checked and no positions fed the automated fit. The first three audits preserve the provisional-model predictions and add predictions from the archival seed at the same visually confirmed coordinates. The f105v local search was initialized by the archival-seed fit. These are physical correspondence checks separate from the exact-seed formal gate.

spatial_resampling.method: Resample occupied 4x4 companion-image cells with replacement, keeping all their validation errors together. No refitting or gate recalculation. Summaries describe sensitivity conditional on the six fitted transformations, and are not confidence intervals for a page's tier.

supplementary_geometry_only.interpretation: On f105v, 31 of 270 held-out matches lie above the tier threshold. Twenty-three exceed 100 QC pixels, and 22 have valid patch windows. All 22 patches correlate better at the predicted position. Some distant matches share the same detected target point. Eighteen of the 23 are still reciprocal nearest descriptors, so simple reciprocity would not remove all aliases. At intermediate distances the original point can have the better-looking patch, especially near the right margin. Both true local geometric errors and repeated-text mismatches remain visible. No held-out matches were removed, no tier was reassigned and the separate blocked and resampling diagnostics do not admit a new comparison.

calibration.definition: Median non-endpoint digital centerline diameter over dominant component height, one value per retained crop. A supporting page-side statistic is the median of its retained crop values. No stroke ratios enter the per-crop eligibility rules.
calibration.method_scope: Synthetic round-capped line assemblies with known constant pen width. Stress is a sensitivity only. Image distortions are illustrative and carry no physical manuscript labels.

reproduction.frozen_geometry_command: python3 rescue_registration.py f33v f108v f111v f37r f103v f105v
reproduction.support_helper: Extract the previous support spec's reproduction.script as ../voynich-mate-support-work/audit_support.py. That source reads the sibling voynich-swarm pinned ZL3b-n.txt. The new support audit reads archive QC tiers and published crop counts directly from the immutable 181-face Yale manifest.

"""Measure full-page Yale registration using identical SIFT matches for both fits."""

import argparse
import hashlib
from importlib.machinery import SourceFileLoader
from importlib.util import module_from_spec, spec_from_loader
import json
from pathlib import Path
import sys

import cv2
import numpy as np
from PIL import Image
from scipy.interpolate import RBFInterpolator
from scipy.spatial import Delaunay, cKDTree

ROOT = Path(__file__).resolve().parent
ARCHIVE_SEED = 440908
MANIFEST = json.loads((ROOT / "archived-yale-summary.json").read_text())["manifest"]
PAGE_SEEDS = {row["page"]: ARCHIVE_SEED + index for index, row in enumerate(MANIFEST, 1)}
ROBUST_RADIUS_QC = 3.0
LOCAL_NEIGHBORS = 48
LOCAL_SMOOTHING = 30.0

loader = SourceFileLoader("archived_registration", str(ROOT / "archived-registration.py"))
spec = spec_from_loader(loader.name, loader)
archive = module_from_spec(spec)
sys.modules[loader.name] = archive
loader.exec_module(archive)


def digest(path):
    return hashlib.sha256(path.read_bytes()).hexdigest()


def project(coordinates, matrix):
    return cv2.perspectiveTransform(coordinates.astype(np.float64)[:, None, :], matrix)[:, 0]


def read_page(page):
    folder = ROOT / "assets" / page
    source = np.asarray(Image.open(folder / "reference.jpg").convert("L"))
    target = np.asarray(Image.open(folder / "yale.jpg").convert("L"))
    native_height, native_width = target.shape
    scale = 1600 / max(native_height, native_width)
    overview = cv2.resize(target, None, fx=scale, fy=scale, interpolation=cv2.INTER_AREA)
    boxes = np.asarray(
        [entry[1:] for entry in json.loads((folder / "boxes.json").read_text())[1]],
        dtype=np.float64,
    )
    return folder, source, overview, target.shape, boxes


def sift_matches(source, overview):
    sift = cv2.SIFT_create(nfeatures=7000, contrastThreshold=0.02)
    left, left_vectors = sift.detectAndCompute(source, None)
    right, right_vectors = sift.detectAndCompute(overview, None)
    pairs = cv2.BFMatcher().knnMatch(left_vectors, right_vectors, k=2)
    matched = [a for a, b in pairs if a.distance < archive.RATIO_THRESHOLD * b.distance]
    return (
        np.asarray([left[item.queryIdx].pt for item in matched], dtype=np.float32),
        np.asarray([right[item.trainIdx].pt for item in matched], dtype=np.float32),
    )


def fit(source, target, train):
    base, inliers = cv2.findHomography(
        source[train], target[train], cv2.RANSAC, archive.RANSAC_THRESHOLD_PX,
    )
    training_source = source[train]
    residual = target[train] - project(training_source, base)
    tree = cKDTree(training_source)
    neighbors = tree.query(training_source, k=min(25, len(train)))[1]
    local_median = np.median(residual[neighbors], axis=1)
    keep = np.linalg.norm(residual - local_median, axis=1) <= ROBUST_RADIUS_QC
    keep_xy, keep_indices = training_source[keep], train[keep]
    warp = RBFInterpolator(
        keep_xy, residual[keep], smoothing=LOCAL_SMOOTHING, neighbors=LOCAL_NEIGHBORS,
    )
    return base, inliers.ravel().astype(bool), warp, keep_indices


def errors_and_metrics(source, target, boxes, train, test, inliers, predictions):
    errors = np.linalg.norm(predictions - target[test], axis=1)
    centers = boxes[:, :2] + boxes[:, 2:] / 2
    hull = Delaunay(source[inliers])
    inside = (hull.find_simplex(centers) >= 0)
    result = {
        "train_matches": int(len(train)),
        "train_inliers": int(len(inliers)),
        "train_inlier_fraction": len(inliers) / len(train),
        "heldout_matches": int(len(test)),
        "heldout_median_error_px": float(np.median(errors)),
        "heldout_p90_error_px": float(np.quantile(errors, 0.9)),
        "heldout_within_5px": float(np.mean(errors <= 5)),
        "box_center_hull_coverage": float(np.mean(inside)),
        "covered_companion_boxes": int(inside.sum()),
        "total_companion_boxes": int(len(boxes)),
    }
    return errors, result


def block_check(source, target, width, height):
    # Hold out full 8-by-8 checkerboard stripes, not adjacent features in the same cell.
    cell = np.minimum(np.floor(source * [8 / width, 8 / height]).astype(int), 7)
    folds = (cell[:, 0] + 2 * cell[:, 1]) % 4
    all_homography_errors, all_rescue_errors = [], []
    for fold in range(4):
        train, test = np.flatnonzero(folds != fold), np.flatnonzero(folds == fold)
        base, _, warp, _ = fit(source, target, train)
        p0 = project(source[test], base)
        p1 = p0 + warp(source[test])
        all_homography_errors.extend(np.linalg.norm(p0 - target[test], axis=1).tolist())
        all_rescue_errors.extend(np.linalg.norm(p1 - target[test], axis=1).tolist())
    return {
        "n_matches": len(all_rescue_errors),
        "homography_p90_qc_px": float(np.quantile(all_homography_errors, 0.9)),
        "rescue_p90_qc_px": float(np.quantile(all_rescue_errors, 0.9)),
    }


def measure(page):
    folder, reference, overview, native_shape, boxes = read_page(page)
    h, w = reference.shape
    source, target = sift_matches(reference, overview)
    train, test = archive._spatial_split(source, w, h, PAGE_SEEDS[page])
    base, linear_inliers, warp, kept = fit(source, target, train)
    initial = project(source[test], base)
    corrected = initial + warp(source[test])
    old_errors, homography = errors_and_metrics(
        source, target, boxes, train, test, train[linear_inliers], initial,
    )
    new_errors, rescue = errors_and_metrics(source, target, boxes, train, test, kept, corrected)
    match_geometry = {
        "source_companion_xy": source.round(4).tolist(),
        "target_overview_xy": target.round(4).tolist(),
        "training_indices": train.tolist(),
        "local_training_indices": kept.tolist(),
        "heldout_indices": test.tolist(),
        "homography": base.tolist(),
        "homography_errors_qc_pixels": old_errors.round(5).tolist(),
        "rescue_errors_qc_pixels": new_errors.round(5).tolist(),
    }
    geometry_path = folder / "registration-matches.json"
    geometry_path.write_text(json.dumps(match_geometry, separators=(",", ":")) + "\n")
    return {
        "page": page,
        "matching_split_seed": PAGE_SEEDS[page],
        **rescue,
        "ratio_matches": int(len(source)),
        "qc_width": overview.shape[1],
        "qc_height": overview.shape[0],
        "native_width": native_shape[1],
        "native_height": native_shape[0],
        "homography_baseline": homography,
        "blocked_comparison": block_check(source, target, w, h),
        "inputs": {
            filename: digest(folder / filename)
            for filename in ("reference.jpg", "yale.jpg", "boxes.json")
        },
        "match_geometry_sha256": digest(geometry_path),
    }


def main():
    parser = argparse.ArgumentParser()
    parser.add_argument("pages", nargs="+")
    args = parser.parse_args()
    cv2.setNumThreads(1)
    cv2.setRNGSeed(ARCHIVE_SEED)
    result = {"method": {
        "opencv_version": cv2.__version__,
        "seed": ARCHIVE_SEED,
        "local_neighborhood_size": LOCAL_NEIGHBORS,
        "local_smoothing": LOCAL_SMOOTHING,
        "training_residual_gate_qc_px": ROBUST_RADIUS_QC,
    }, "faces": []}
    for page in args.pages:
        row = measure(page)
        result["faces"].append(row)
        print(json.dumps(row), flush=True)
    (ROOT / "registration-results.json").write_text(json.dumps(result, indent=2) + "\n")


if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()
scripts_as_text.diagnose_registration.py:
"""Diagnose existing held-out descriptor matches without changing the gate."""

from collections import Counter
import argparse
import json
from pathlib import Path

import numpy as np
from PIL import Image, ImageDraw
from scipy.interpolate import RBFInterpolator
from scipy.ndimage import gaussian_filter, map_coordinates
from rescue_registration import read_page, project, LOCAL_NEIGHBORS, LOCAL_SMOOTHING


ROOT = Path(__file__).resolve().parent


def corr(a, b):
    a = a - a.mean()
    b = b - b.mean()
    denominator = np.linalg.norm(a) * np.linalg.norm(b)
    return float(a @ b / denominator) if denominator > 0 else 0.0


def diagnose(page):
    folder, source_raster, target_raster, _, _ = read_page(page)
    geometry = json.loads((folder / "registration-matches.json").read_text())
    source = np.asarray(geometry["source_companion_xy"])
    target = np.asarray(geometry["target_overview_xy"])
    train = np.asarray(geometry["local_training_indices"])
    test = np.asarray(geometry["heldout_indices"])
    base = np.asarray(geometry["homography"])
    warp = RBFInterpolator(
        source[train], target[train] - project(source[train], base),
        smoothing=LOCAL_SMOOTHING, neighbors=LOCAL_NEIGHBORS,
    )
    source_xy, raw_target = source[test], target[test]
    predicted = project(source_xy, base) + warp(source_xy)
    shifted = [
        project(source_xy + shift, base) + warp(source_xy + shift) - predicted
        for shift in (np.array([1, 0]), np.array([0, 1]))
    ]
    jacobian = np.stack(shifted, axis=1)
    height, width = source_raster.shape
    tgt_height, tgt_width = target_raster.shape
    errors = np.linalg.norm(raw_target - predicted, axis=1)
    y, x = np.mgrid[-9:10, -9:10]
    offsets = np.column_stack((x.ravel(), y.ravel()))
    source_gray = source_raster.astype(float)
    target_gray = target_raster.astype(float)
    source_high = source_gray - gaussian_filter(source_gray, 2.0)
    target_high = target_gray - gaussian_filter(target_gray, 3.0)

    def in_bounds(points, width, height):
        return (points[:, 0].min() >= 0 and points[:, 0].max() < width - 1
                and points[:, 1].min() >= 0 and points[:, 1].max() < height - 1)

    def get(raster, coords):
        return map_coordinates(raster, [coords[:, 1], coords[:, 0]], order=1)

    patches = {}
    out_of_frame = 0
    for index, (s, raw, guess) in enumerate(zip(source_xy, raw_target, predicted, strict=True)):
        source_points = s + offsets
        target_offsets = offsets @ jacobian[index]
        raw_points, guess_points = raw + target_offsets, guess + target_offsets
        if not (
            in_bounds(source_points, width, height)
            and in_bounds(raw_points, tgt_width, tgt_height)
            and in_bounds(guess_points, tgt_width, tgt_height)
        ):
            out_of_frame += 1
            continue
        a = get(source_high, source_points)
        b = get(target_high, raw_points)
        c = get(target_high, guess_points)
        patches[index] = {
            "matched_qc_error_px": float(errors[index]),
            "archive_descriptor_patch_correlation": corr(a, b),
            "registered_patch_correlation": corr(a, c),
            "source_xy": s.tolist(),
            "claimed_qc_xy": raw.tolist(),
            "registered_qc_xy": guess.tolist(),
        }
    values = list(patches.values())
    bins = [
        ("at_most_1", 0, 1),
        ("above_1_to_2", 1, 2),
        ("above_2_to_20", 2, 20),
        ("above_20_to_100", 20, 100),
        ("above_100", 100, float("inf")),
    ]
    result = {
        "folio": page,
        "heldout": len(test),
        "patch_out_of_frame": out_of_frame,
        "gross_above_100_px": int(sum(errors > 100)),
        "bins": {},
        "audit_sample": {},
    }
    audit = []
    for key, low, high in bins:
        sample = [
            (i, row) for i, row in patches.items()
            if low < row["matched_qc_error_px"] <= high
        ]
        if not sample:
            continue
        _, rows = zip(*sample, strict=True)
        deltas = [
            row["registered_patch_correlation"] - row["archive_descriptor_patch_correlation"]
            for row in rows
        ]
        result["bins"][key] = {
            "available_pairs": len(rows),
            "n_more_correlated_at_registered_position": sum(delta > 0 for delta in deltas),
            "median_descriptor_correlation": float(np.median([
                row["archive_descriptor_patch_correlation"] for row in rows
            ])),
            "median_registered_correlation": float(np.median([
                row["registered_patch_correlation"] for row in rows
            ])),
        }
        ranked = sorted(sample, key=lambda pair: pair[1]["matched_qc_error_px"])
        selected = sorted(set(np.rint(np.linspace(0, len(ranked) - 1, min(4, len(ranked)))).astype(int)))
        for i in selected:
            index, row = ranked[i]
            audit.append((index, key))
            result["audit_sample"][str(index)] = row
    canvas = Image.new("L", (600, 43 + 64 * len(audit)), color=238)
    pen = ImageDraw.Draw(canvas)
    pen.text((8, 8), f"{page} / companion patch, archive match, registered prediction", fill=0)
    for row, (index, key) in enumerate(audit):
        s, raw, guess = source_xy[index], raw_target[index], predicted[index]
        target_offsets = offsets @ jacobian[index]
        y0 = 38 + 64 * row
        for x0, pixels in zip((10, 67, 124), (
            get(source_gray, s + offsets),
            get(target_gray, raw + target_offsets),
            get(target_gray, guess + target_offsets),
        ), strict=True):
            block = Image.fromarray(pixels.clip(0, 255).astype(np.uint8).reshape(19, 19))
            canvas.paste(block.resize((51, 51), Image.Resampling.NEAREST), (x0, y0))
        v = patches[index]
        pen.text((184, y0 + 10), f"{index:03}  {key}  error {errors[index]:.2f} QC px", fill=0)
        pen.text((184, y0 + 26), f"image correlation {v['archive_descriptor_patch_correlation']:.2f} / {v['registered_patch_correlation']:.2f}", fill=0)
    canvas.save(folder / "heldout-match-diagnostic.jpg", quality=92)
    return result


def main():
    parser = argparse.ArgumentParser()
    parser.add_argument("pages", nargs="+")
    args = parser.parse_args()
    report = {page: diagnose(page) for page in args.pages}
    (ROOT / "diagnostic-results.json").write_text(json.dumps(report, indent=2) + "\n")
    print(json.dumps({page: data["bins"] for page, data in report.items()}, indent=2))


if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()

"""Measure reciprocal SIFT consistency as a descriptive diagnostic only."""
import json
from collections import Counter
from pathlib import Path

import cv2
import numpy as np
from rescue_registration import archive, read_page


ROOT = Path(__file__).resolve().parent


def inspect(page):
    folder, reference, target, _, _ = read_page(page)
    sift = cv2.SIFT_create(nfeatures=7000, contrastThreshold=0.02)
    left, left_vectors = sift.detectAndCompute(reference, None)
    right, right_vectors = sift.detectAndCompute(target, None)
    matcher = cv2.BFMatcher()
    forward = [
        first for first, second in matcher.knnMatch(left_vectors, right_vectors, k=2)
        if first.distance < archive.RATIO_THRESHOLD * second.distance
    ]
    backward = {result.queryIdx: result.trainIdx for result in matcher.match(right_vectors, left_vectors)}
    geometry = json.loads((folder / "registration-matches.json").read_text())
    split = geometry["heldout_indices"]
    errors = np.array(geometry["rescue_errors_qc_pixels"])
    source = np.array([left[match.queryIdx].pt for match in forward])
    target = np.array([right[match.trainIdx].pt for match in forward])
    assert np.allclose(source, geometry["source_companion_xy"], atol=0.0001)
    assert np.allclose(target, geometry["target_overview_xy"], atol=0.0001)
    mutual = np.array([
        backward[forward[index].trainIdx] == forward[index].queryIdx for index in split
    ])
    targets = Counter(forward[index].trainIdx for index in split)
    duplicated_target = np.array([targets[forward[index].trainIdx] > 1 for index in split])
    bins = {}
    for label, mask in {
        "at_most_1_qc_px": errors <= 1,
        "above_1_through_20_qc_px": (errors > 1) & (errors <= 20),
        "above_20_through_100_qc_px": (errors > 20) & (errors <= 100),
        "above_100_qc_px": errors > 100,
    }.items():
        bins[label] = {
            "count": int(mask.sum()),
            "mutual_descriptor_top_matches": int((mask & mutual).sum()),
            "reused_target_keypoint": int((mask & duplicated_target).sum()),
        }
    return bins


def main():
    cv2.setNumThreads(1)
    pair = {page: inspect(page) for page in ("f103v", "f105v")}
    (ROOT / "reciprocal-diagnostic.json").write_text(json.dumps(pair, indent=2) + "\n")
    print(json.dumps(pair, indent=2))


if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()

"""Summarize tier sensitivity to spatial resampling of the frozen validation matches."""

import json
from pathlib import Path

import numpy as np

ROOT = Path(__file__).resolve().parent
THRESHOLD = 1.8199963569641113
REPEATS = 4000
SEED = 71805


def resample(page):
    path = ROOT / "assets" / page / "registration-matches.json"
    geometry = json.loads(path.read_text())
    source = np.array(geometry["source_companion_xy"])[geometry["heldout_indices"]]
    errors = np.array(geometry["rescue_errors_qc_pixels"])
    indices = np.minimum((source * [4 / 636, 4 / 900]).astype(int), 3)
    cell_ids = indices[:, 0] + 4 * indices[:, 1]
    blocks = [errors[cell_ids == i] for i in sorted(set(cell_ids))]
    rng = np.random.default_rng(SEED)
    samples = []
    for pick in rng.integers(0, len(blocks), size=(REPEATS, len(blocks))):
        sample = np.concatenate([blocks[index] for index in pick])
        samples.append(np.quantile(sample, 0.90))
    return {
        "heldout_count": len(errors),
        "populated_cells": len(blocks),
        "observed_p90_qc_px": float(np.quantile(errors, 0.9)),
        "resampled_p90_qc_px_quantiles_10_50_90": np.quantile(samples, [0.1, 0.5, 0.9]).tolist(),
        "resamples_above_frozen_cutoff": int(sum(value > THRESHOLD for value in samples)),
    }


def main():
    results = {
        "simulations_each": REPEATS,
        "seed": SEED,
        "threshold": THRESHOLD,
        "method": "Resample occupied 4x4 companion-image cells with replacement, keeping all their validation errors together. No refitting or gate recalculation. Summaries describe sensitivity conditional on the six fitted transformations, and are not confidence intervals for a page's tier.",
        "faces": {
            page: resample(page)
            for page in ("f33v", "f108v", "f111v", "f37r", "f103v", "f105v")
        },
    }
    (ROOT / "registration-tier-resampling.json").write_text(json.dumps(results, indent=2) + "\n")
    print(json.dumps(results, indent=2))


if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()
scripts_as_text.calibrate_stroke.py:
"""Calibrate a dimensionless ink-width measurement on generated line shapes.

Run with Python 3, NumPy and SciPy. No image files are read by the CLI.
The same ``measure_crop`` function can later accept a grayscale crop supplied
by a separate, blinded image procedure.
"""

import argparse
from collections import Counter
from hashlib import sha256
import json
from pathlib import Path

import numpy as np
import scipy
from scipy import ndimage as ndi


QC = {
    "min_crop_side_px": 20,
    "denoise_sigma_px": 0.45,
    "dark_quantile": 0.01,
    "light_quantile": 0.85,
    "min_contrast": 0.20,
    "threshold_fraction_from_dark": 0.50,
    "min_ink_fraction": 0.008,
    "max_ink_fraction": 0.55,
    "min_dominant_ink_fraction": 0.80,
    "edge_clearance_px": 2,
    "min_component_height_px": 18,
    "skeleton_upsampling": 2,
    "min_centerline_samples_px": 10,
}
DIMS = (3, 4, 6, 8, 10)
SCALES = (0.65, 1.0)
PHASES = ((0.23, 0.61), (0.72, 0.31))
SUPERSAMPLE = 6
MARGIN_PX = 9
BASE_SEED = 180621
REGIMES = {
    "clean": {"blur_sigma_px": 0.0, "noise_sd": 0.0, "gradient": 0.0, "ink": 0.13},
    "degraded": {"blur_sigma_px": 0.85, "noise_sd": 0.035, "gradient": 0.10, "ink": 0.22},
    "stress": {"blur_sigma_px": 1.30, "noise_sd": 0.060, "gradient": 0.16, "ink": 0.33},
}
GATES = {
    "clean": {"min_retention": 0.90, "max_median_relative_error": 0.08,
              "max_p90_relative_error": 0.18},
    "degraded": {"min_retention": 0.85, "max_median_relative_error": 0.125,
                 "max_p90_relative_error": 0.24},
}
SHAPES = {
    "straight": (((14, 8), (14, 64)),),
    "inclined": (((9, 8), (30, 64)),),
    "hook": (((12, 8), (12, 39), (14, 50), (19, 59), (28, 63), (36, 62)),),
    "serpentine": (((15, 8), (22, 16), (25, 25), (23, 34), (15, 44), (12, 53), (16, 64)),),
    "fork": (((16, 64), (16, 33), (12, 20), (7, 8)), ((16, 33), (22, 22), (28, 10))),
}


def _neighbors(mask):
    padded = np.pad(mask, 1)
    return (
        padded[:-2, 1:-1], padded[:-2, 2:], padded[1:-1, 2:], padded[2:, 2:],
        padded[2:, 1:-1], padded[2:, :-2], padded[1:-1, :-2], padded[:-2, :-2],
    )


def _sum_indicators(items):
    return np.add.reduce(items, axis=0, dtype=np.uint8)


def _thin(mask):
    """Zhang–Suen thinning, DOI 10.1145/357994.358023."""
    centerline = mask.copy()
    changed = True
    while changed:
        changed = False
        for phase in (0, 1):
            adj = _neighbors(centerline)
            north, _, east, _, south, _, west, _ = adj
            count = _sum_indicators(adj)
            rises = _sum_indicators([~a & b for a, b in zip(adj, adj[1:] + adj[:1])])
            if phase == 0:
                blocked = (north & east & south) | (east & south & west)
            else:
                blocked = (north & east & west) | (north & south & west)
            remove = centerline & (2 <= count) & (count <= 6) & (rises == 1) & ~blocked
            changed |= bool(np.any(remove))
            centerline[remove] = False
    return centerline


def measure_crop(gray):
    """Measure one dominant dark component from a grayscale crop in [0, 1].

    The 2× raster thinned centerline estimates the ink medial axis. The median
    diameter is twice the Euclidean distance to the nearest background sample
    at its non-endpoint pixels, converted back to native pixel units. One crop
    contributes one width-to-component-height ratio if all fixed QC rules pass.
    """
    gray = np.asarray(gray, dtype=float)
    if gray.ndim != 2 or min(gray.shape) < QC["min_crop_side_px"]:
        return {"kept": False, "reason": "crop_too_small_or_not_grayscale"}
    if not np.isfinite(gray).all() or gray.min() < 0 or gray.max() > 1:
        return {"kept": False, "reason": "invalid_input_range"}

    smooth = ndi.gaussian_filter(gray, QC["denoise_sigma_px"], mode="nearest")
    dark, light = np.quantile(smooth, [QC["dark_quantile"], QC["light_quantile"]])
    contrast = float(light - dark)
    if contrast < QC["min_contrast"]:
        return {"kept": False, "reason": "low_contrast", "contrast": contrast}
    threshold = dark + QC["threshold_fraction_from_dark"] * contrast
    ink = smooth < threshold
    fraction = float(ink.mean())
    if not QC["min_ink_fraction"] <= fraction <= QC["max_ink_fraction"]:
        return {"kept": False, "reason": "ink_fraction_out_of_range", "ink_fraction": fraction}

    components, _ = ndi.label(ink, structure=np.ones((3, 3), dtype=bool))
    sizes = np.bincount(components.ravel())[1:]
    winner = int(np.argmax(sizes))
    dominance = float(sizes[winner] / sizes.sum())
    if dominance < QC["min_dominant_ink_fraction"]:
        return {"kept": False, "reason": "no_dominant_component", "dominance": dominance}

    y_span, x_span = ndi.find_objects(components)[winner]
    clearance = min(y_span.start, x_span.start, gray.shape[0] - y_span.stop, gray.shape[1] - x_span.stop)
    if clearance < QC["edge_clearance_px"]:
        return {"kept": False, "reason": "component_touches_crop_margin", "clearance_px": clearance}
    height = y_span.stop - y_span.start
    if height < QC["min_component_height_px"]:
        return {"kept": False, "reason": "component_too_short", "component_height_px": height}

    mask = components[y_span, x_span] == winner + 1
    scale = QC["skeleton_upsampling"]
    grid = np.pad(np.repeat(np.repeat(mask, scale, axis=0), scale, axis=1), 1)
    centerline = _thin(grid)
    inner = centerline & (_sum_indicators(_neighbors(centerline)) >= 2)
    samples = int(np.count_nonzero(inner))
    if samples < QC["min_centerline_samples_px"] * scale:
        return {"kept": False, "reason": "centerline_too_short", "centerline_samples": samples}
    width = float(2 * np.median(ndi.distance_transform_edt(grid)[inner]) / scale)
    return {"kept": True, "ratio": width / height, "stroke_width_px": width,
            "component_height_px": height, "centerline_samples": samples,
            "contrast": contrast, "ink_fraction": fraction, "dominance": dominance,
            "clearance_px": clearance}


def _raster(paths, width, scale, phase):
    """Supersample the union of line segments with round caps and joins."""
    width *= scale
    shift = np.asarray(phase)
    paths = [np.asarray(path) * scale + shift for path in paths]
    vertices = np.concatenate(paths)
    left_top = np.floor(vertices.min(axis=0) - width / 2 - MARGIN_PX).astype(int)
    right_bottom = np.ceil(vertices.max(axis=0) + width / 2 + MARGIN_PX).astype(int)
    columns, rows = right_bottom - left_top
    xx = (np.arange(columns * SUPERSAMPLE) + 0.5)[None, :] / SUPERSAMPLE + left_top[0]
    yy = (np.arange(rows * SUPERSAMPLE) + 0.5)[:, None] / SUPERSAMPLE + left_top[1]
    covered = np.zeros((rows * SUPERSAMPLE, columns * SUPERSAMPLE), dtype=bool)
    for path in paths:
        for (x0, y0), (x1, y1) in zip(path, path[1:]):
            dx, dy = x1 - x0, y1 - y0
            step = np.clip(((xx - x0) * dx + (yy - y0) * dy) / (dx * dx + dy * dy), 0, 1)
            covered |= (xx - x0 - step * dx) ** 2 + (yy - y0 - step * dy) ** 2 <= (width / 2) ** 2
    coverage = covered.reshape(rows, SUPERSAMPLE, columns, SUPERSAMPLE).mean(axis=(1, 3))
    truth_height = float(np.ptp(vertices[:, 1]) + width)
    return coverage, width, truth_height


def _capture(coverage, regime, seed):
    plane = 0.88 + regime["gradient"] * np.linspace(-0.5, 0.5, coverage.shape[0])[:, None]
    gray = plane * (1 - coverage) + regime["ink"] * coverage
    gray = ndi.gaussian_filter(gray, regime["blur_sigma_px"], mode="nearest")
    rng = np.random.default_rng(seed)
    pixels = gray + rng.normal(0, regime["noise_sd"], gray.shape)
    return np.rint(np.clip(pixels, 0, 1) * 255) / 255


def _summary(rows):
    retained = [r for r in rows if r["measurement"]["kept"]]
    errors = {"ratio_abs": [], "ratio_relative": [], "width_px_abs": [], "height_px_abs": [], "ratio_bias": []}
    for r in retained:
        m = r["measurement"]
        delta = m["ratio"] - r["true_ratio"]
        errors["ratio_abs"].append(abs(delta))
        errors["ratio_relative"].append(abs(delta) / r["true_ratio"])
        errors["width_px_abs"].append(abs(m["stroke_width_px"] - r["true_width_px"]))
        errors["height_px_abs"].append(abs(m["component_height_px"] - r["true_height_px"]))
        errors["ratio_bias"].append(delta)
    return {
        "specimens": len(rows), "retained": len(retained), "retention": len(retained) / len(rows),
        "rejected": dict(Counter(r["measurement"]["reason"] for r in rows if not r["measurement"]["kept"])),
        "median_errors": {k: float(np.median(v)) if v else None for k, v in errors.items()},
        "p90_errors": {k: float(np.quantile(v, 0.90)) if v else None for k, v in errors.items()},
    }


def _reject_cases():
    blank = np.full((64, 64), 0.88)
    low_contrast = blank.copy()
    low_contrast[10:54, 30:34] = 0.77
    clipped = blank.copy()
    clipped[:54, 30:34] = 0.13
    disconnected = blank.copy()
    disconnected[10:54, 21:25] = 0.13
    disconnected[12:56, 39:43] = 0.13
    short = blank.copy()
    short[23:37, 25:33] = 0.13
    return {
        "blank": (blank, "low_contrast"),
        "low_contrast": (low_contrast, "low_contrast"),
        "clipped": (clipped, "component_touches_crop_margin"),
        "disconnected": (disconnected, "no_dominant_component"),
        "short": (short, "component_too_short"),
    }


def calibrate():
    rows = []
    for name, paths in SHAPES.items():
        for nominal_width in DIMS:
            for scale in SCALES:
                for phase in PHASES:
                    coverage, true_width, true_height = _raster(paths, nominal_width, scale, phase)
                    for regime_name, capture in REGIMES.items():
                        seed = BASE_SEED + len(rows)
                        measure = measure_crop(_capture(coverage, capture, seed))
                        rows.append({"shape": name, "nominal_width_px": nominal_width, "scale": scale,
                                     "phase": phase, "regime": regime_name, "seed": seed,
                                     "true_width_px": true_width, "true_height_px": true_height,
                                     "true_ratio": true_width / true_height, "measurement": measure})
    by_regime = {n: _summary([r for r in rows if r["regime"] == n]) for n in REGIMES}
    resolution = {
        name: {width: _summary([r for r in rows if r["regime"] == name and test(r["true_width_px"])])
               for width, test in (("under_3_px", lambda w: w < 3), ("at_least_3_px", lambda w: w >= 3))}
        for name in REGIMES
    }
    checks = {}
    for name, gates in GATES.items():
        summary = by_regime[name]
        error = summary["median_errors"]["ratio_relative"]
        p90 = summary["p90_errors"]["ratio_relative"]
        checks[name] = bool(summary["retention"] >= gates["min_retention"] and error is not None
                            and error <= gates["max_median_relative_error"]
                            and p90 <= gates["max_p90_relative_error"])
    rejection_checks = {}
    for name, (image, expectation) in _reject_cases().items():
        observed = measure_crop(image)
        rejection_checks[name] = {"expected_reason": expectation, "measurement": observed,
                                  "pass": observed.get("reason") == expectation}
    checks["rejection_cases"] = all(v["pass"] for v in rejection_checks.values())
    return {
        "definition": "Median non-endpoint digital centerline diameter over dominant component height, one value per retained crop. A supporting page-side statistic is the median of its retained crop values. No stroke ratios enter the per-crop eligibility rules.",
        "references": {"thinning": "https://doi.org/10.1145/357994.358023",
                       "distance": "https://docs.scipy.org/doc/scipy/reference/generated/scipy.ndimage.distance_transform_edt.html"},
        "method_scope": "Synthetic round-capped line assemblies with known constant pen width. Stress is a sensitivity only. Image distortions are illustrative and carry no physical manuscript labels.",
        "settings": {"crop_qc": QC, "regimes": REGIMES, "gate_thresholds": GATES,
                     "shapes_xy": SHAPES, "widths_px_at_scale_one": DIMS, "scales": SCALES,
                     "pixel_phases_xy": PHASES, "supersampling": SUPERSAMPLE, "margin_px": MARGIN_PX,
                     "base_seed": BASE_SEED, "noise_rng": "NumPy default_rng (PCG64)"},
        "implementation": {"numpy": np.__version__, "scipy": scipy.__version__,
                           "script_sha256": sha256(Path(__file__).read_bytes()).hexdigest()},
        "passes_gates": all(checks.values()), "gates": checks, "regime_summary": by_regime,
        "summary_by_true_width_class": resolution, "rejection_checks": rejection_checks, "specimens": rows,
    }


def main():
    parser = argparse.ArgumentParser(description=__doc__)
    parser.add_argument("--out", type=Path, default=Path(__file__).with_name("calibration.json"))
    args = parser.parse_args()
    result = calibrate()
    args.out.write_text(json.dumps(result, indent=2, allow_nan=False) + "\n", encoding="utf-8")
    print(json.dumps({"gates": result["gates"], "regimes": result["regime_summary"]}, indent=2))


if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()
scripts_as_text.check_visual_geometry.py:
"""Compare independently recorded landmarks with the exact-seed transforms."""

import json
from pathlib import Path

import numpy as np
from scipy.interpolate import RBFInterpolator
from rescue_registration import project, LOCAL_NEIGHBORS, LOCAL_SMOOTHING


ROOT = Path(__file__).resolve().parent


def main():
    exact = json.loads((ROOT / "registration-seed-exact.json").read_text())
    faces = {row["page"]: row for row in exact["faces"]}
    for page in ("f33v", "f108v", "f111v"):
        source_file = ROOT / f"manual-landmark-audit-{page}.json"
        output = json.loads(source_file.read_text())
        metric = faces[page]
        p = ROOT / "assets" / page / "registration-matches.json"
        geometry = json.loads(p.read_text())
        reference = np.array(geometry["source_companion_xy"])
        target = np.array(geometry["target_overview_xy"])
        train = np.array(geometry["local_training_indices"])
        h = np.array(geometry["homography"])
        residual = target[train] - project(reference[train], h)
        correct = RBFInterpolator(
            reference[train], residual, smoothing=LOCAL_SMOOTHING, neighbors=LOCAL_NEIGHBORS,
        )
        positions = np.array([row["reference"] for row in output["rows"]])
        observed = np.array([row["yale_native"] for row in output["rows"]])
        projected = (project(positions, h) + correct(positions)) * [
            metric["native_width"] / metric["qc_width"],
            metric["native_height"] / metric["qc_height"],
        ]
        errors = np.linalg.norm(observed - projected, axis=1)
        for row, xy, err in zip(output["rows"], projected, errors, strict=True):
            row["automatic_exact_seed_yale_native"] = xy.round(3).tolist()
            row["exact_seed_difference_native_px"] = round(float(err), 3)
        output["exact_seed"] = metric["matching_split_seed"]
        output["exact_seed_median_p90_max_native_px"] = [
            float(np.median(errors)), float(np.quantile(errors, 0.9)), float(errors.max()),
        ]
        (ROOT / f"manual-landmark-exact-{page}.json").write_text(json.dumps(output, indent=2) + "\n")
        print(page, output["exact_seed_median_p90_max_native_px"])


if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()
